flagship.headline: MC5 begin recording Kick Out the Jams in Detroit
flagship.summary_line_1: MC5 began recording their debut album Kick Out the Jams live at the Grande Ballroom in Detroit on October 30, 1968, the first of two nights, per Louder.
flagship.summary_line_2: Elektra's live album reached No. 30 on the Billboard 200, and the clip below is the title track.

events.headline: Marvin Gaye releases I Heard It Through the Grapevine
events.summary_line_1: Tamla released Marvin Gaye's single I Heard It Through the Grapevine, backed with You're What's Happening (in the World Today), on October 30, 1968, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 on the chart dated December 14, 1968, and stayed there for seven weeks, and the clip below is the single version.

events.headline: Brian Jones is sentenced to nine months in prison
events.summary_line_1: Brian Jones of the Rolling Stones admitted drug possession in court on October 30, 1967, and was sentenced to nine months in prison, per Songfacts.
events.summary_line_2: A London appeals court overturned the sentence on December 12, 1967, and the clip below is the Stones' 1967 single We Love You.

events.headline: The Beatles play two shows at the Gaumont in Bournemouth
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played two shows at the Gaumont Cinema in Bournemouth on October 30, 1964, on their autumn UK tour, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Both shows used the same ten-song set, and the clip below is A Hard Day's Night, which was on it.

events.headline: The Beatles tape Drop In for Swedish television
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles taped an appearance on the Swedish television show Drop In in Stockholm on October 30, 1963, the day after their last Swedish concert, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: Producer Klas Burling talked them into one song beyond the planned She Loves You and Twist and Shout, and the clip below is She Loves You.
